plan.title: The Cartographer's Bargain
plan.premise: Slender, a young dwarf fighter, carries a torn map—his late father's last gift—that shows a land that should not exist on any chart. Three regions on the map are blank where they should be settled, and marked where they should be empty. Wherever Slender travels, the land reshapes itself to match the map, and the map redraws itself after him. Something is drawing the world and redrawing it, and Slender is being walked toward a final page. The map is not a record of the land; it is a contract with the one who signs it last.
plan.theme: A living map that erases and redraws the world, and the bargain of being remembered by it

acts.title: The Inkwood Fringe
acts.goal: Follow the map's first blank margin to a lost border village, and learn why the forest keeps rewriting its own name.

region.name: The Inkwood Fringe
region.flavour: A border forest where old road-signs are found with the letters smeared off, and travelers swear the trees lean toward anyone carrying paper.

arrival.name: Fogplot Crossroads
arrival.flavour: A three-way junction with a leaning guidepost whose letters run like wet ink whenever anyone reads them aloud.

spokes.name: Millbrook Thoroughfare
spokes.flavour: A mossy wooden bridge over a slow stream, its planks replaced so often no two boards are the same wood.

spokes.name: Hollow Charter Oak
spokes.flavour: A vast hollow oak strung with hundreds of faded paper strips, each a lost name, rustling like trapped birds.

spokes.name: Mothlight Dell
spokes.flavour: A clearing where pale moths cluster so thickly on bark that the trees appear to burn white in the dusk.

gateway.name: Lastmile Stead
gateway.flavour: A burnt-out homestead at the map's edge where the ground is soft as wet paper and the chimney stands like a quill.

boss.name: Signless Barrow
boss.ally_path: The Barrow's keeper is not evil—it is a forgotten scribe who will stand down if shown a written name it once recorded (the Charter Oak holds such a name for the party). Show the name and it lowers its blade to hear what it forgot.

acts.title: The Salted Slate
acts.goal: Cross the map's second blank mark—a drowned swampland—to reach the tower where the map's maker once lived.

region.name: The Salted Slate
region.flavour: A salt-stained swamp where the water mirrors the sky so perfectly that wading feels like walking on a map of clouds.

arrival.name: Bluewash Landing
arrival.flavour: A quiet ferry point where the current runs backwards at certain hours and no boatman will take coin for the crossing.

spokes.name: Saltmirror Fen
spokes.flavour: Shallow black water stretches to the horizon, perfectly still, reflecting travelers as older or younger with no pattern.

spokes.name: Glumroot Burrows
spokes.flavour: A warren of collapsed bank-holes where the mud smells of iodine and deep digging tools lie abandoned by the dozen.

spokes.name: Weeper's Causeway
spokes.flavour: A raised stone path that shifts underfoot, its old carvings weeping brine that stings any fresh wound.

gateway.name: The Unfinished Tower
gateway.flavour: A leaning tower of stacked slate, never roofed, whose interior is scribbled floor-to-ceiling with fading draughtsman's marks.

boss.name: Margrave Vell
boss.ally_path: Vell hoards not gold but maps, and craves a single lost chart the party can offer. If they surrender their own torn map (or a convincing copy), Vell will bargain instead of burn, and may even point the way onward.

acts.title: The Final Page
acts.goal: Reach the map's last unmarked place—a buried keep of living stone—and face the one who has been rewriting the world, choosing memory or erasure.

region.name: The Cartolith Vault
region.flavour: A subterranean keep carved from pale living stone that slowly reshapes its own walls, corridors closing and opening like a page turning.

arrival.name: The Margin Gate
arrival.flavour: A broad stone threshold where all sound falls suddenly silent, and every footstep leaves a faint gray mark behind.

spokes.name: Vellum Halls
spokes.flavour: Endless halls hung with dried hide sheets, some blank, others stitched over with corrections that bleed through from behind.

spokes.name: The Redraft Gallery
spokes.flavour: A long room where stone statues stand mid-erasure, half their features worn smooth as if the sculptor gave up.

spokes.name: Binding Chasm
spokes.flavour: A deep fissure crossed by a single stone ribbon, beneath which flows a river of black ink that never reaches the walls.

gateway.name: The Cartolith
gateway.flavour: A domed vault where the living map is stitched into the stone itself, breathing, its lines redrawing as you watch.

boss.name: The Last Cartographer
boss.ally_path: The Cartographer does not wish to harm Slender—it wishes to be remembered, and has mistaken his father's map for a promise. If the party offers a name to be written into the Cartolith (their own, willingly), the giant will cease rewriting the world and grant them a final page. Refusal means a fight

npcs.name: Old Kern Boltnose
npcs.demeanor: Gruff and paper-skinned, squints at every traveler's boots first.
npcs.motive: Wants to know whose hand wrote the graffiti now appearing on his guidepost by dawn.

secrets.text: Kern has been secretly re-lettering the guidepost nightly, terrified the names will point travelers to a village that no longer exists.
Kern buried a small iron coffer of 'the old surveyors' pins' behind the Charter Oak; the pins can temporarily pin a map's lines still.

npcs.name: Mara The Windvane
npcs.demeanor: Restless, speaks in gusts, never faces the same direction twice.
npcs.motive: Seeks the name her mother tore off the family tree before vanishing.

secrets.text: Mara's missing mother was the last keeper of the Signless Barrow, and died refusing to let its name be erased.
Mara knows the map redraws itself only for those carrying paper—and that Slender's map is slowly using his own breath as ink.

npcs.name: Pontiff Wren Osbeck
npcs.role: Lapsed survey-priest of the Salted Slate
npcs.demeanor: Soft-spoken, wrings his hands, apologizes for the salt in the air.
npcs.motive: Needs the Unfinished Tower's original blueprints to atone for a betrayal that sank his temple.

secrets.text: Wren is the one who burned the Lastmile Stead years ago, trying to destroy a map he thought cursed.
The reversed current at Bluewash Landing is the ink-river of the Cartolith backing up through the earth—proof the vault is near.

npcs.name: Gleb Half-Page
npcs.demeanor: All hoods and wet coughs, sells maps from a coat that chimes with folded tin.
npcs.motive: Wants Slender's torn map to sell to the highest bidder, and will poison the well if refused cleanly.

secrets.text: Gleb works for Margrave Vell, feeding the wyrmling maps so it won't turn its hunger to the living of the Slate.
Gleb carries a forgery of Slender's father's signature; he's been testing whether the map obeys forged hands.

npcs.name: Aulder Runegraft
npcs.role: Stone-carver and reluctant keeper of the
npcs.demeanor: Measured, patient, but his eyes dart to the walls as if they might move.
npcs.motive: Guards the gate to repay a debt to the Last Cartographer, who once spared his family from erasure.

secrets.text: Aulder secretly carves a small notch in the Margin Gate for every traveler who passes; he keeps the count to remember them when the vault tries to forget.
The Last Cartographer is not a villain but a prisoner of its own craft—it can only stop rewriting the world if a living name is written into the Cartolith.

quests.title: The Nameless Bough
quests.objective: Recover a folded strip bearing her mother's name from among the hundreds hanging in the Hollow Charter Oak.

quests.title: Signs Without Signposts
quests.objective: Find who is re-lettering the Fogplot guidepost each night and make them stop—or stand with them.

quests.title: Salt Under the Nails
quests.objective: Cross the reversed current at Bluewash Landing and retrieve the original blueprints from a caved chamber beneath the Unfinished Tower.

quests.title: Ransom of the Mirrorwater
quests.objective: Steal a chart from Margrave Vell's hoard without waking the wyrmling, and hand it to Gleb—or sell Vell a forgery instead.

quests.title: A Debt of Passage
quests.objective: Persuade Aulder that the Last Cartographer can be freed without more erasure, and win entry past the Margin Gate.

rival.hook: Gleb trails Slender one map-margin behind, buying up every chart that changes, and will reach the Cartolith last—unless Slender's map, which Gleb covets, changes hands first.

event.text: A three-way junction with a leaning guidepost whose letters run like wet ink whenever anyone reads them aloud.

The crossroads warp the light beneath the leaning post, and Old Kern Boltnose already has an eye on your boots before either of you speaks. He names himself tollkeeper of Fogplot Crossroads, then offers two tasks in the same breath: a hunt for lost signage, and another for a nameless bough. His papery fingers tap the post once, and the letters smear like tears before settling back into unreadable script.

summary.text: The crossroads warp the light beneath the leaning post, and Old Kern Boltnose already has an eye on your boots before either of you speaks.
summary.title: At Fogplot Crossroads

fact.text: Quest The Nameless Bough is offered.
Quest Signs Without Signposts is offered.

event.text: You are at Fogplot Crossroads. A three-way junction with a leaning guidepost whose letters run like wet ink whenever anyone reads them aloud. Here with you: Old Kern Boltnose (Tollkeeper of Fogplot Crossroads). Ways on: Millbrook Thoroughfare, Hollow Charter Oak and Mothlight Dell.

event.reason: Carefully searching the crossroads and the leaning guidepost for anything hidden or noteworthy

feature.name: Loose Stone Brick
feature.description: A brick at the guidepost's base sits a hair proud of the others, its mortar freshly crumbled. Behind it, a small hollow holds a folded scrap of oilcloth.

fact.text: Slender's careful search of Fogplot Crossroads revealed a loose brick at the guidepost's base hiding a hollow with a folded scrap of oilcloth tucked inside.

event.text: Slender’s careful sweep of the guidepost’s base finds one brick riding proud of its neighbors, its mortar still shedding grit. A firm nudge shifts it loose, revealing a small hollow behind, where a folded scrap of oilcloth waits in the dark. Old Kern watches with a squint, saying nothing, though his papery fingers tap once against his belt.
Slender works the loose brick fully free with a scrape of crumbling mortar, then pinches the folded oilcloth from the hollow and opens it. The moment passes, and the world waits for what you do next.

fact.text: Slender unfolded the oilcloth scrap from the hollow at the guidepost's base and read what was written on it.

event.text: Slender unfolds the oilcloth with care, the waxy scrap soft and nearly translucent in the warped light of the guidepost. Scratched into its surface with charcoal, not ink, is a shaky drawing of a leaning post and a hollow brick, with an arrow curled back toward the crossroads themselves. Old Kern cranes his neck, still silent, though the creak of his spine is plain even from a pace away. The cloth holds no words, only that crude circle and arrow, as if the message was never meant to be read aloud at all.

event.reason: Attacking Old Kern Boltnose is a point of no return: they will fight back. Confirm?

event.text: Old Kern’s squint sharpens into something mean, and before either of you can step back, his papery hand darts toward the oilcloth in your grip. The fight is brief and ugly: a flurry of bony knuckles, a scraping boot-heel, and the dull ring of your shield as you put the old tollkeeper down in the dust at the base of the post. He sprawls there, breathing hard, one arm twisted beneath him, his pouch spilled open at his side. The oilcloth lies untouched in your hand, its crude arrow still circling back toward the crossroads.

Slender steps off the packed earth of the crossing, boots scraping through dry grass as he moves toward the shallow ravine that cuts along the junction's eastern edge. The ground slants quickly, loose pebbles rolling ahead of him as he descends a few feet into the gully. Nothing waits down there but the smell of old leaves and the sound of Old Kern's labored breathing somewhere behind and above. The guidepost's warped light does not follow him far; the ravine sits in a gray, windless dimness. No new feature reveals itself, and no path opens from that low ditch except the way you came.

Old Kern’s mouth works once, a soundless curse or a plea, then his eyes roll back and his head lolls against the packed earth. The dust around his sprawled body begins to settle, and the only movement left is the slow uncurling of one papery hand beside the spilled pouch. The guidepost’s runny letters gleam for a heartbeat in the warped light, then dim as if the crossroads has turned its face away from the body at its foot. The ravine’s gray quiet presses up behind you, and the tollkeeper’s gold lies scattered where it fell, waiting for whoever stands.

summary.text: Slender prised a loose brick from the base of the guidepost at Fogplot Crossroads and drew a folded scrap of oilcloth from the hollow behind it, which bore only a charcoal drawing of the post and a hollow brick with an arrow curling back toward the crossroads. Old Kern Boltnose then lunged for the oilcloth, and Slender struck him down in a brief scuffle, leaving the tollkeeper sprawled and dying at the foot of the post with his pouch spilled open. Slender briefly descended the shallow ravine at the junction's eastern edge and found nothing there but the way he had come. Old Kern's eyes rolled back and he went still, his scattered gold lying where it fell.
summary.title: Tollkeeper felled at the crossroads

fact.text: Slender recovered a folded oilcloth scrap from the hollow behind the loose stone brick, bearing a crude charcoal drawing of the guidepost, a hollow brick and a coiled arrow rather than words.
Old Kern Boltnose attacked Slender over the oilcloth and was beaten down; he lies dying or dead at the guidepost's base.
Old Kern's spilled pouch and scattered gold lie at the foot of the guidepost, unclaimed.
The shallow ravine on the junction's eastern edge holds nothing and offers no path except the way back up to the crossroads.

event.text: Slender kneels beside the still body of Old Kern Boltnose, and the scattered gold glints dully as you gather it coin by coin into the spilled pouch. The dust clings to your fingers, and the pouch is lighter than it looked when it hung from the tollkeeper’s belt. The gathered coins settle against the oiled leather with a faint chime, and the crossroads grow quiet around you. The guidepost’s runny letters shimmer once, then still. At the base of the post, the loose brick lies where you left it, and the hollow behind it shows only shadow now.

Slender stoops and takes up the spilled pouch, the oiled leather cool against your fingers and the gathered gold shifting faintly inside. The crossroads hold their breath around you; Old Kern lies still at the guidepost’s base, and the runny letters above him dim to a dull shine. The pouch hangs as lightly from your grip as it must have from his belt, and the hollow brick behind the post shows only shadow where the oilcloth once waited. Nothing else moves at Fogplot Crossroads.

event.reason: Examining the loose stone brick and its hollow for anything missed

event.text: Slender kneels once more at the guidepost’s base, fingers tracing the loose stone brick where the mortar has crumbled fresh. You tilt it toward the warped light, turn it over, and peer into the hollow behind, but the angle only shows the same gritty shadow and the faint scrape marks where the oilcloth once rested. The runny letters above you shimmer and blur, making the light shift just enough to trick your eyes, and for a heartbeat the hollow seems deeper than it is. The brick sits heavy and ordinary in your hands, its edges rough with old mortar, and no hidden mark or second cache reveals itself. Old Kern lies still at the post’s foot, and the spilled pouch remains where you set it, its gathered gold catching the dim light. The hollow behind the stone is empty, only dust and the faint imprint of the oilcloth that is no longer there.
